N1_fences_back_to_literal_lf._note: The pre-#4453 plugin predicate. Every CRLF axis reddens on every surface; the BOM+LF cases stay green, and that asymmetry is what proves the two halves of the fix are separately load-bearing. X2 reddens because an unrecognised block is 'no block at all', so the malformed file is reported as an invariant violation instead of an unparseable-frontmatter skip — the silent-drop class #4439/#4440 closed. ⛤ C5 also reddens once it exists, and the reason is read rather than smoothed over: with an LF-only predicate `frontmatterBlockBody(CRLF)` is null, so C5 ends up comparing js-yaml's parse of nothing against the LF mapping. Same class as the other corrections in this PR (integration-test-revert-verify §A44) — the expectation had been written before C5 was added, from the mutant's theme rather than from which axes execute after it lands.

N2_bom_never_skipped._note: Type-preserving (still a number), so a BROKEN verdict cannot be mistaken for redness. Only the BOM axes redden: C2 is pure-CRLF, P4 and X2 use CRLF-only fixtures, C4's controls are unaffected.

N3_predicate_loses_its_start_anchor._note: Guards the OVER-WIDENING direction — the class #4439's review caught once already. Without `^`, a `---` fence inside the BODY is read as the asset's frontmatter, and the doubled-BOM file becomes visible through its SECOND fence. Narrow by construction: C4 is the only axis carrying shapes that must stay unrecognised.

N4_body_gets_its_carriage_returns_stripp._note: The plausible 'helpful' normalisation, rejected on purpose: stripping would silently rewrite user content AND make the returned offsets stop matching the returned text. Narrow by construction — C2 is the only axis that asserts the body verbatim. ⛤ C5 added after the review of PR #4458: it asserts the same decision on a REAL YAML implementation (js-yaml) rather than on the hand-rolled Obsidian double, whose `\r` tolerance is incidental. N4 reddens both — C2 on the bytes, C5 on the parse.

N5_offsets_ignore_the_bom._note: Keeps the BOM out of the MATCH but points the offsets at index 0, so a future write path splicing [blockStart, blockEnd) would eat the byte. Not reachable from today's read-only plugin call sites, which is exactly why it needs its own axis rather than relying on one.
